issues.detail: The Greek 'παρακλητον εχομεν' (we have an advocate) is rendered as 'chúng ta có Đấng Yên Ủi' (we have a Comforter/Consoler). In the context of 1 John 2:1, 'παράκλητος' refers to an Advocate or Intercessor. While 'Yên Ủi' can be used for Paraclete, it often leans toward 'Comforter'. However, the more critical issue is the scope of the advocacy.
The Greek specifies that the advocate is 'προς τον πατερα' (toward/before the Father). The Vietnamese 'ở nơi Cha' (in the Father) slightly shifts the location/direction of the advocacy.
